clue.text: Make up lies about Conservative without delay

indicators.note: lies about means one word sits around another, as a body lies about a spot

parts.note: to make up for a wrong is to atone

explanation.surface: Someone instantly invents falsehoods about a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' looks like inventing the lies, but it means making amends; 'lies about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean immediately, straight away.

clue.text: An element essential to unicellular gonococci

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chemical element is vital to single-celled gonorrhoea bacteria.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas, number 18 in the periodic table, is one chemical element.

clue.text: Chicken and pork with new stuffing eaten by playwright

indicators.note: eaten by means the stuffed pork goes inside the playwright's name

parts.note: Joe Orton was an English playwright of the 1960s

indicators.note: stuffing means the letter for new is packed inside the word for pork

parts.note: pork is the meat of a pig

explanation.surface: A playwright dines on chicken and pork with a new stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new stuffing' suggests a cook's recipe but packs the letter for new into the pork word. The Orpington is a British breed of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy domestic fowl breed named after a town in Kent is a kind of hen.

clue.text: Time is ignored by island tribe

indicators.note: is ignored by means the island's name leaves out the letter for time

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: An island tribe pays no attention to the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of Canada and the northern USA, so a tribe.

clue.text: One riding bay's swell initially moving ahead? He's no sailor

indicators.note: moving ahead means that letter shifts to the front of the rider's word

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse, so whoever rides one is a horseman

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of swell

explanation.surface: Someone on horseback watches the bay's swell move forward and admits he is no seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests the sea, but it is the horse; the S of HORSEMAN, picked out as the first letter of 'swell', moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who works or lives on land by the coast is a landsman, not someone who goes to sea.

clue.text: Describes people sporting their halo, regularly enough to upset?

definitions.text: Describes people sporting their halo, regularly enough to upset?

indicators.note: upset means all the gathered letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of enough, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People who parade their haloes often enough to annoy everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'enough' gives NUH; with THEIR HALO and TO, 'upset' rearranges them. The whole clue also describes the sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: A smug, self-righteous attitude: those who flaunt their virtue as if saintlier than everyone else.

clue.text: Restaurant is not last in line to go under — rubbish!

indicators.note: to go under means, in this down clue, the remaining letters sit below the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: not last means the final letter of the word for line is dropped

parts.note: a series is a line or succession of things

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea that a restaurant is not the last in line to go bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go under' suggests going bankrupt; it places IS and SERIE beneath ROT in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: An eating house specialising in spit-roasted meat is a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Grass skirts from Zimbabwe found after a month in France

indicators.note: found after means these letters come behind the French month

parts.note: Mai is the French name for May

indicators.note: skirts from means the outer edges of the word Zimbabwe, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Grass skirts from Zimbabwe turn up in France a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass skirts' reads as one item of clothing; split it, and 'skirts' becomes the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is a cereal crop belonging to the grass family.

clue.text: Headless rider on horse could appear in one?

definitions.text: Headless rider on horse could appear in one?

indicators.note: on means, in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second
headless means the first letter of the rider's word is dropped

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior, a rider
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A headless horseman is just the sort of thing to haunt a bad dream.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a headless rider is the stuff of a terrifying dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A frightening dream, where a headless horseman might well turn up.

clue.text: Firmly take in hand a stingy sort, though it's unpleasant?

definitions.text: Firmly take in hand a stingy sort, though it's unpleasant?

parts.words: Firmly take in hand a stingy sort, though it's unpleasant
parts.note: literally, seize a stinging plant firmly in the fist; figuratively, tackle a difficult task boldly and without delay

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to deal firmly with a mean-spirited person, unpleasant as that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stingy' suggests a miser, but here it means something that stings: a weed whose sting is said to be blunted if gripped hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means confronting a difficulty boldly, from the belief that a stinging weed held tightly will not hurt.

clue.text: Chance to gain experience before going up a pay grade, possibly? Not nowadays

definitions.text: Chance to gain experience before going up

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of a pay grade are to be rearranged

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era, so it stands for nowadays

explanation.surface: An opportunity to gain experience before promotion to a higher pay band, though such chances no longer exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' sounds like promotion but is the British phrase for starting university. 'Not' takes the letters AD out of A PAY GRADE before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A year out between school and university, often spent travelling or working, gives young people experience.

clue.text: Being a landlord, about to acquire tenant's first money

indicators.note: to acquire means the word for about takes in the other pieces

parts.note: read as a bout: one stage of a contest, such as a leg of a match

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of tenant is used

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A landlord is about to collect the first rent from a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' must be split as 'a bout', a round or stage of a contest; the setter later admitted the device was a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Renting property out to others is what a landlord does.

clue.text: Italian composer's a subject to avoid

definitions.meaning: Luigi, the Venetian avant-garde composer of the twentieth century
a taboo topic, something that should not be done or mentioned

explanation.surface: An Italian composer is a topic best steered clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of a modernist Venetian composer; the other is a taboo, a thing forbidden.

clue.text: Extremely scrupulous staff involved in property valuation

indicators.note: involved in means these letters are taken inside the word for property

parts.note: an asset is a piece of property

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of scrupulous, its first and last letters

parts.note: men are the staff or workforce

explanation.surface: Very careful staff are engaged in valuing a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'scrupulous', but it selects that word's first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal or estimate of worth, as of property for tax.

clue.text: Plant exotic flowers or do without flora at first?

indicators.note: exotic signals that the letters of flowers or do are rearranged
at first means only the opening letter of flora

explanation.surface: Is a plant an exotic flower, or does it manage without flora at all?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the F, first letter of 'flora', from FLOWERS OR DO before 'exotic' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A small woodland herb with clover-like leaves is a plant.

clue.text: Trait of criminal, being gripped by heartless thirst for revenge

indicators.note: being gripped by means the rearranged letters sit inside the remaining outer letters
heartless means the middle of thirst is removed, leaving its first and last letters
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of trait of are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal is consumed by a cold-hearted thirst for vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TRAIT OF to ITFORTA, which goes between the T and T left of 'thirst'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation in kind, repaying an injury with a like one, is a form of vengeance.

clue.text: Delilah's work for a while: what contributed to Samson's strength?

parts.note: to temp is to do temporary work
Samson's strength lay in his uncut hair, so a lock of it contributed

explanation.surface: Delilah's brief job: discovering the source of Samson's might.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Delilah seduces Samson and has his hair cut off, robbing him of his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Philistine woman who seduced Samson is the archetypal seductress.

clue.text: Injection of water to clean ground meant mostly end to famine

indicators.note: end to means only the final letter of famine
ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
mostly means the last letter of meant is cut off

explanation.surface: Ground water injected to clean the soil was mostly meant to end a famine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MEANT to MEAN, which 'ground' rearranges to follow the E from the end of 'famine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectal injection of fluid used to flush out the bowels.

clue.text: European worried securing work in New York is complicated

indicators.note: securing means the outer pieces hold the American work word inside them

parts.note: ate means worried or troubled, as in what's eating you
labor is the American spelling of labour, work

explanation.surface: A worried European takes a job in New York, and it is complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in New York' signals the American spelling LABOR, without the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate and detailed, with many parts, as an involved plan is.

clue.text: Taken into care, goose at last laid eggs

indicators.note: taken into means the chosen letter goes inside the word for care

parts.note: to mind is to look after or care for

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of goose

explanation.surface: A goose taken into care finally lays eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eggs' is old military slang for mines or bombs, so to lay eggs is to place mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Planting explosive charges at sea or on land is laying them, and those charges are slangily called eggs.

clue.text: Destroy using constant penetrating energy beam

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: penetrating means the constant's letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to beam is to radiate, to send out rays
c is the symbol for the speed of light, a physical constant

explanation.surface: A weapon destroys by firing a steady, piercing energy beam.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely, root and branch.

clue.text: Colour gold's alien to artist

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
or is the heraldic word for gold
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter finds the colour gold foreign to his work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance painter Jacopo Robusti was a great artist.

clue.text: Heartless relative joins resistance and becomes more likeable

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the relative's word is removed

parts.note: a niece is a relative
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted relative joins the Resistance and becomes better liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasanter, more agreeable to be around.

clue.text: Scoundrel's in front of English magistrate

indicators.note: in front of means the scoundrel's word comes before the next letter

parts.note: a dog is a rogue or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain comes before an English magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The magistrate is not a court official here but the elected ruler of old Venice or Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief magistrate of the former republics of Venice and Genoa.

clue.text: Old pew's cut up with axes — this may stick it together

indicators.note: up means, in this down clue, the old and the cut pew are read upwards
cut means the last letter of pew is removed

parts.note: a pew is a church bench
x and y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: An old church bench is chopped up with axes; glue might mend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' are not choppers but the X and Y axes of a graph; 'up' turns O and PE to EPO.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin adhesive that sets hard is a strong glue.

clue.text: Bored? Entertainment ultimately would be handy

parts.note: bored is fed up, read as an instruction for this down clue: the word fed written upwards

indicators.note: ultimately means only the last letter of entertainment

explanation.surface: Bored? Some entertainment at last would come in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'Bored' stands for FED UP, which in a down clue means FED written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful and dexterous with the hands.

clue.text: Passage runs into bar

indicators.note: into means the letter for runs goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A short passage runs into a bar of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a noun; it is the preposition meaning excluding.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract or quoted section of a text is a passage.

clue.text: Egon Ronay finishes off stew — this gave it flavour?

indicators.note: stew means the remaining letters are cooked up into a new order
finishes off means the last letter of each name is removed

explanation.surface: A food critic polishes off a stew and credits a herb for its flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: Egon Ronay was a famous British restaurant critic and guide writer; dropping each name's last letter leaves EGO RONA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb used in cooking adds taste to a dish such as a stew.

clue.text: One going along leisurely in streetcar?

parts.note: the word splits as street, abbreviated ST
the word's second half is car, and a Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce car

explanation.surface: A rider ambling along in a tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streetcar' must be split into 'street' and 'car'; a Roller is British slang for a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking a leisurely walk, sauntering along.

clue.text: Arch embodying support that's firm

indicators.note: embodying means the word for arch contains the word for support

parts.note: arch means cunning or roguish, so sly
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: An arch that contains a support is a sturdy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like a structure but is the adjective meaning knowing and mischievous.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and resolute, unyielding like metal.
